items_missed: No agenda opener at the top of the call — jumped straight from greeting to availability; the 'here's what we'll cover, takes 10-15 minutes' framing and the explicit 'sound good?' confirmation never happened (the mid-call 'I'm gonna go over pricing and the estimate' is not the Section 1 opener)

Never recapped the quote form or confirmed the details on file — customer referenced 'I saw that on your thing' but Chris never confirmed origin/destination addresses or zips; only asked for the office unit number (111)
No stairs/floors/elevator question at either location — the origin is a unit in an office building and the destination is her house, and this drives both time and crew safety

Never pinned down the 'insanely heavy' item — customer said something heavy but 'not 600 lbs' and Chris only replied 'those are very heavy.' No weight, dimensions, or specialty-equipment follow-up on the single biggest estimate risk in the job
No special-considerations probe — long walks, narrow hallways, tight turns, parking at the office building
No moving-stressors question ('anything you're particularly worried about?')

No Worries Damage Coverage never explained — 'insurance' was listed as included in the rate but the $2,000 repair/replace/reimburse coverage and the 60¢/lb baseline were never mentioned, on a call with an unusually heavy item
On-Time Guarantee never mentioned — he gave a 1:30-3:30 arrival window and a 30-minute courtesy call but never the guarantee behind it
Full 'no hidden fees' pitch not delivered — 'includes absolutely everything' is a summary, not the no credit card fees / no transportation fees / no fuel surcharge / no assembly fees list
No sense-check after the clock explanation ('does that make sense?') — the whole pricing/clock/estimate block was delivered as one uninterrupted paragraph
Save Your Ass prep speech absent — no consolidation tips on the loose office contents, no 'take a carload' suggestion, no close
Walk distance and traffic never raised as estimate variables on a Friday-afternoon cross-town office move
No deposit was only addressed reactively — customer had to ask 'do you need a credit card or something to hold it?' It was never proactively pitched as a differentiator
Email handoff was named but not explained — no mention of the bolded detail list at the top or 'reply with any corrections'
Never asked 'any other questions before I let you go?' and never gave hours or how to reach the team
Used the customer's name once, and got it wrong ('Hey, Jenny' — customer is Geni)
top_strength: Excellent real-time re-qualification: he opened with a date problem ('we're fully booked up for the twenty eighth'), heard it was only a few furniture items, and immediately reversed to 'well that changes things, we might be able to get you in on the twenty eighth' — then asked for the booking directly and steered her to the earlier window specifically so the possible extra stop wouldn't push the crew into the evening.
coaching_note: Chris ran the mechanics well but skipped every trust-builder that isn't about price. On a job where the customer volunteered that one item is 'insanely heavy,' the No Worries $2,000 coverage was the single most relevant thing he could have said, and he said only the word 'insurance' inside the inclusions list. Pair that with the missing weight/stairs/walk-distance questions on an office-unit pickup and he quoted a flat $555 with no idea whether two movers can actually get that piece out. Next call: when a customer flags a heavy or unusual item, stop and probe it (weight, dimensions, stairs, walk), then use it as the natural bridge into No Worries, Meet Your Mover, and the On-Time Guarantee.
phone_presence_notes: Warm, adaptive, and light on his feet — 'making this easy on us,' 'oh, dropping — yeah, that's super easy' — and the customer stayed upbeat through the close ('sounds great, thank you so much'), though he used her name only once and got it wrong.
